question.text: Ms. Priya Shah runs the Satpura 130/30 Long-Short Fund with Investable Funds of INR 400 crore. She deploys the classic 130/30 allocation. What is the GROSS exposure and NET exposure of the fund?

explanation.text: The Logic: A 130/30 strategy is 130% long + 30% short. Gross = 130 + 30 = 160% (INR 640 cr). Net = 130 - 30 = 100% (INR 400 cr). Section 10.1.1.2 explicitly states net exposure equals 100% of investable funds. The Trap: Option C is a common confusion that adds only one leg. Option A ignores the short leg. Option B confuses net and gross in the wrong direction. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Equity Derivatives) tests gross/net exposure arithmetic. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) requires explaining net-vs-gross to HNIs; XIX-E is the manager-side construction view. Manager's Pro-Tip: At 160% gross, you're already at 1.6x leverage; you have only 0.4x cushion under the SEBI 2x Cat III cap. A market stress that swings your Put hedges can breach the cap — pre-approve an intraday deleverage script with the prime broker.
